instrument_name: MGL c.151 s.1 Minimum fair wage
figure_or_rule_carried: Minimum wage 15.00 USD/h (any occupation); in no case less than 0.50 USD above the effective federal minimum (federal 7.25 -> floor 7.75, not binding). No indexation in the text; no 2027 rate enacted in the section.

instrument_name: MGL c.151 s.1A Overtime
figure_or_rule_carried: Overtime 1.5x regular rate above 40 hours per work week (no daily overtime). Commissions, drawing accounts, bonuses and sales/production incentive pay excluded from the regular rate. Retail Sunday/holiday hours paid at 1.5x under c.136 excluded from the overtime count. Exemptions (1)-(20) incl. executive/administrative/professional earning > 80 USD/week, outside sales, seasonal (<=120 days), fishermen, seamen, etc.

instrument_name: MGL c.151 s.7 Service rate for tipped employees
figure_or_rule_carried: Tipped employees (> 20 USD/month in tips): cash wage not less than 6.75 USD/h plus tip credit up to the s.1 wage (15.00 - 6.75 = 8.25 USD/h max credit, derived); top-up computed at completion of each shift; employee must be informed and retain all tips (pooling among tipped employees allowed). Janitor/caretaker with living quarters: not less than 36 USD/week.
verification_method: inspected directly (statute text read); tip credit derived arithmetically

instrument_name: MGL c.151 s.2A Agricultural minimum wage
figure_or_rule_carried: Agriculture and farming: minimum wage 8.00 USD/h, except a child 17 or under or an immediate family member of the employer; commissioner may fix fair value of board/lodging. Federal FLSA minimum 7.25 may still apply where FLSA covers (FED unit).

instrument_name: MGL c.151 s.15 Payroll records
figure_or_rule_carried: Employer keeps name, address, occupation, amount paid each pay period, hours worked each day and week; retain at least 3 years after entry; employee may inspect own records at reasonable times.

instrument_name: MGL c.149 s.148C Earned sick time
figure_or_rule_carried: 1 hour per 30 hours worked from hire; use from 90th calendar day; FLSA 213(a)(1) exempt employees deemed 40 h/week; employers with 11+ employees (full-time, part-time, temporary counted): up to 40 h PAID per calendar year at the same hourly rate (not below c.151 s.1 minimum); smaller employers: 40 h unpaid; carry-over up to 40 h but use capped at 40 h/year; no payout on separation. Purposes include pregnancy loss / failed assisted reproduction, adoption or surrogacy (c)(5). Cities/towns covered only if accepted locally. Notice rule in (o) already registered as US-MAL-002.

instrument_name: MGL c.149 s.27B Prevailing wage certified payroll
figure_or_rule_carried: Public works (ss.26-27A): contractor/subcontractor keeps name, address, classification, hours, wages per worker; submits certified payroll WEEKLY to the awarding authority (mail or e-mail) with signed statement; attach apprentice ID copy each week; keep 3 years from contract completion; statement of compliance within 15 days after completion of its work. No dollar threshold in s.27B.

instrument_name: MGL c.62E s.2 New-hire reporting duty
figure_or_rule_carried: Employers (incl. governmental entities) and labor organizations notify DOR of each hire; payors notify DOR of contractor agreements; also retirements with a retirement allowance and workers' compensation claims; timing, form and data fixed by commissioner regulation.

instrument_name: MGL c.246 s.28 Wage exemption from trustee process
figure_or_rule_carried: Ordinary creditor wage attachment: exempt per week = greater of 85% of gross wages or 50 x the greater of federal or MA hourly minimum wage (50 x 15.00 = 750 USD/week, derived); more protective than CCPA 25%. Not applicable to divorce, separate maintenance or child support orders: federal CCPA support limits apply instead. ERISA/401(a)/403(b)/IRA pensions exempt.
verification_method: inspected directly (statute text read); 750 USD derived arithmetically

instrument_name: MGL c.175M s.6 PFML contributions
figure_or_rule_carried: Contribution rates adjusted annually (s.7(e)); medical leave: employee deduction max 40% of contribution; family leave: up to 100%; employers < 25 MA employees: no employer share, remit 100% family + 40% medical from employees (consolidated text as served 2026-11-02; the 2027 swap by Chapter 101 of the Acts of 2026 is not reflected in this text, see US-MAS5-012); no contribution on wages above the Social Security contribution and benefit base (42 USC 430).

instrument_name: MGL c.175M s.3 PFML benefit amount
figure_or_rule_carried: 7-calendar-day waiting period (employee may use accrued employer paid leave in it); weekly benefit 80% of AWW up to 50% of SAWW + 50% above; maximum weekly benefit re-set by DFML by Oct 1 each year to 64% of SAWW, effective Jan 1 (indexation). Reduced by other wage replacement (WC, other disability).

instrument_name: DFML - PFML employer contribution rates and calculator (2026 and 2027)
authority: Massachusetts Department of Family and Medical Leave
figure_or_rule_carried: 2026: 25+ covered individuals 0.88% of eligible wages = family 0.18% (up to 100% from employee) + medical 0.70% (employee up to 40% = 0.28%, employer 60% = 0.42%); < 25: 0.46% (family 0.18 + medical 0.28, all withholdable, no employer share). 2027 (Chapter 101 of the Acts of 2026, eff. 2027-01-01): 25+: family 0.70% (employee up to 40% = 0.28%, employer 0.42%), medical 0.18% (up to 100% from employee) -> total 0.88%; < 25: 0.46%. Individual contributions capped at the Social Security taxable maximum. Rate applies to wages earned on/after Jan 1.
verification_method: quoted from authority page; totals derived arithmetically (0.28+0.42+0.18=0.88)

instrument_name: DOR Withholding Tax Guide (posted August 2026)
figure_or_rule_carried: Withhold from residents (services in or outside MA) and nonresidents (services in MA); non-MA employer with MA office: MA amount minus own-state amount; no federal withholding required -> no MA withholding (household employers generally not required, optional). New employees complete W-4 and M-4; no M-4 -> zero exemptions; decrease -> new M-4 within 10 days; exemptions only with principal employer. Percentage method: wages minus FICA/Medicare/MA-US-RR retirement contributions (annual max 2,000) minus exemption amount (daily 3n+9; weekly 19n+66; biweekly 38n+131; semimonthly 42n+141; monthly 83n+284; annual 1,000n+3,400) x withholding rate; HoH/blind reductions weekly 2.31/2.12, biweekly 4.62/4.23, semimonthly 5.00/4.58, monthly 10.00/9.17, daily 0.33/0.30. Return/payment: <=100 annual (Jan 31); 101-1,200 quarterly; 1,201-25,000 monthly by 15th (Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec due last day of next month); >25,000 quarterly return + payment within 3 business days when >=500 accumulated by 7th/15th/22nd/last day. E-file mandatory: new registrations, payroll service providers, combined liability >=5,000. Records 3 years. New hires within 2 weeks; contractors >=600. W-2 to employees by Jan 31. Page also states 50+ employees file W-2 machine-readable by last day of March and paper W-2 + M-3/M-3M by Feb 28 (CONFLICTS with US-MAS5-015). Penalties late pay/file 1%/month max 25%; interest federal short-term + 4%; 5% deposit penalty for >25,000 filers.

instrument_name: DOR Form M-4 Massachusetts Employee's Withholding Exemption Certificate
figure_or_rule_carried: Lines: 1 personal exemption (1, or 2 if 65+); 2 spouse (4, or 5 if spouse 65+); 3 qualified dependents; 4 total exemptions; 5 additional withholding per pay period. Boxes: A head of household; B blind; C spouse blind and not subject to withholding; D full-time student in seasonal/part-time/temporary employment with estimated annual income <= 8,000 USD -> employer does not withhold. No certificate -> withhold on zero exemptions. Edition/revision date not found in extracted text (open question).

instrument_name: DOR Form W-2 Responsibilities for Employers (updated 2026-01-30)
figure_or_rule_carried: Who files: MA employers; non-MA employers with MA office/business paying MA residents or nonresidents working in MA; any employer withholding MA tax voluntarily. By Jan 31: W-2 to employee, to SSA and to DOR. 49 or fewer W-2s may file on paper with Form M-3 (mail by Jan 31, PO Box 7015 Boston 02204); 50 or more must upload electronically (MassTaxConnect bulk file, max 250 MB; 'DOR uses a W-2 file format', see Electronic Filing Specifications Handbook). Amendments only on paper with federal W-2c (PO Box 7030). Prior-year W-2s: 50+ electronically.

instrument_name: DOR Report New Hires
authority: Massachusetts Department of Revenue (Child Support Services)
figure_or_rule_carried: Report new employees and independent contractors within 14 days of first day of work (also rehires after 30+ days off payroll). Data: FEIN, legal name, payroll address; employee full name, mailing address, work status (employee/contractor), SSN exactly as on card (no ITIN), first day of employment or reinstatement. 25+ employees must file online via MassTaxConnect (individual or batch text file per New Hire Record Layout); <25 may use Form NHR by mail (PO Box 55141 Boston 02205-5141) or fax 617-376-3262. Multistate employers may report all hires to MA online after registering with OCSE.

instrument_name: Trial Court Law Libraries - Massachusetts law about minimum wage
figure_or_rule_carried: Confirmation: 15.00 USD/h since 2023-01-01 was the final step of the 5-year schedule; no further increases planned unless by legislature or ballot; service rate 6.75; agricultural 8.00; municipal employees excluded from c.151 (opinion MW-02-13-02 citing c.41 s.108A), federal minimum applies to them; au pairs covered (Capron v. AG, 944 F.3d 9 (1st Cir. 2019)).
verification_method: second independent authority (law library vs statute US-MAS5-001)

instrument_name: DUA - Submit employment and wage detail report
figure_or_rule_carried: Quarterly employment and wage detail report due by 3 p.m. Apr 30 / Jul 31 / Oct 31 / Jan 31 (payment by 5 p.m. same dates); filed by employer or TPA in Unemployment Services for Employers; upload CSV, EFW2 or ICESA (single or bulk). Data: Employer Account Number (EAN); employee SSN and full name; hours worked; gross wages; wages subject to withholding; state income tax withheld; work location; 12th-of-the-month employment; adjustment reason code. Wages reported when paid (cash basis), incl. tips, bonuses, separation pay, reasonable cash value of board/lodging, non-cash payments.

instrument_name: DOR Form W-2 Electronic Filing Specifications (Rev. 20191219)
figure_or_rule_carried: Based on SSA EFW2; upload through MassTaxConnect or Bulk File Portal (SFTP, separate registration); PDF and CSV not acceptable; paper only for 49 or fewer W-2s with Form M-3. RA key fields: submitter name, EIN (must match MassTaxConnect user EIN), address. RE: employer EIN, name, address; positions 3-6 tax year; 7 agent indicator (1 = 2678 agent, 2 = common paymaster). RS: only records with MA-taxable wages; key fields SSN, last name, state taxable wages (positions 276-286), state income tax withheld (positions 287-297). RT positions 10-24 = sum of RS state wages; 25-39 = sum of RS state withholding (DOR reconciles). Handbook says it is reissued every tax year, but the edition served on 2026-11-02 is Rev. 20191219 (stale; see open question).
verification_method: inspected directly (PDF text extracted, record positions read)

instrument_name: DUA - 2026 UI and COVID-19 Recovery Assessment Rate Schedule (PDF, text copy)
figure_or_rule_carried: Text-extractable copy of the same document as US-MAP9W-003 (previously read only as viewer screenshots). Schedule E 2026: UI 0.94% (positive reserve 17.0%+) to 14.37% (negative 23%+); COVID-19 Recovery Assessment 0.178% to 2.716%; effective 1.118% to 17.086%. Every band checked: UI + COVID = effective rate (no mismatch). Base: first 15,000 USD per employee (c.151A s.14, US-MA-P5-1-005).
verification_method: inspected directly (PDF text extracted); band sums derived arithmetically

instrument_name: DUA - Employer Medical Assistance Contribution (EMAC)
figure_or_rule_carried: EMAC on the first 15,000 USD of each employee's calendar-year wages (as reported on the quarterly wage detail report). Current rates: years 1-3 exempt; year 4: 0.12%; year 5: 0.24%; year 6+: 0.34%. Exempt: fewer than 6 employees in a quarter; employers newly subject to UI (usually first 3 years). Closes the P7 gap on US-MAP7-002 (0.12%/0.24% first-step rates). Page shows no effective date ('current rates').
verification_method: quoted from authority page; second independent authority to statute row US-MAP7-002 for 0.34%

instrument_name: DUA - Employer contributions to unemployment (local copy)
figure_or_rule_carried: Re-verification with local file of US-MA-P5-1-004 / US-MAP9W-001. Liability: 1+ employee one day a week in 13 weeks, or 1,500 USD wages in any quarter; agricultural 40,000 USD in a quarter or 10+ employees 20 weeks; domestic 1,000 USD cash wages in a quarter; out-of-state employers 200 USD MA gross wages in a quarter. Exempt wages: children under 18 working for parents, spouse, own children, some religious organizations, work-training, real-estate/insurance commissions. 2026: new employers (<3 years) 2.42%; new construction 6.08%; established per schedule. Rate notices by Jan 31; rate review before Jun 20; deferral up to 34% of Q1-Q2 contributions; late interest 12%. Quarterly due 3 p.m. Apr 30/Jul 31/Oct 31/Jan 31.

instrument_name: 830 CMR 62B.2.1 Withholding of Taxes on Wages and Other Payments (local copy)
figure_or_rule_carried: Re-verification with local file of US-MA-P5-1-002 (that row had no local file). (4)(a)1: employers maintaining an office or transacting business in MA withhold on wages taxable to residents or nonresidents; employers without MA office/business may withhold for MA residents as a convenience on request. (8): wages may, at the employer's election, be computed to the nearest dollar. (9)(a): one exemption certificate across concurrent employers; joint/related employers may aggregate, pro-rata liability. (9)(b): MA resident with other-state (or DC, territory, Canada/province) withholding: withhold MA amount less the other jurisdiction amount (credit method).

instrument_name: DOR Circular M 2026 - G-DERIVE check of the wage-bracket table
article_or_section: Weekly table p.2; percentage method p.12 (Rev. 12/25)
figure_or_rule_carried: Same file as US-MA-P5-1-003 (byte-identical to the wayback copy, re-downloaded 2026-11-02 and discarded). Derivation: weekly bracket 150-160, midpoint 155, less FICA 7.65% (11.86) = 143.14; exemptions as ANNUAL factor / 52 (1 = 4,400/52; 2 = 5,400/52), x 5%: 0 ex 7.16, 1 ex 2.93, 2 ex 1.96, 3 ex 1.00 = table exactly. The percentage-method rounded weekly factor (19n+66) gives 2.91 and 1.01 (differences up to 0.02 USD): the two DOR methods are not identical, both allowed. Table notes: claimed spouse counts as 4 exemptions; full-time student <= 8,000 USD: do not withhold; MSRRA exemption with Form M-4-MS: do not withhold.

instrument_name: DFML - How PFML weekly benefit amounts are calculated and/or changed
authority: Massachusetts Department of Family and Medical Leave
article_or_section: SAWW and maximum weekly benefit; last updated 2026-10-09
figure_or_rule_carried: 2026: SAWW 1,922.48 USD, maximum weekly benefit 1,230.39 USD; 2027: SAWW 2,007.20 USD, maximum weekly benefit 1,284.61 USD (both = 64% of SAWW, re-derived exactly). Benefit year = Sunday before first leave day, 52 weeks; caps 20 weeks medical, 12 weeks family, 26 combined. Optional withholding from benefits: 5% state, 10% federal (benefit-side, paid by DFML, not employer payroll). 7-day waiting period may be covered by employer PTO.
verification_method: quoted from authority page; maximum = 64% x SAWW derived arithmetically

instrument_name: Chapter 101 of the Acts of 2026 (FY2026 supplemental budget, H.5470)
figure_or_rule_carried: Status: ENACTED, in force (emergency preamble). Payroll-relevant: s.25-26 swap the c.175M s.6 employee-deduction caps (medical 40% -> 100%, family 100% -> 40%); s.45 says ss.25-26 'apply for taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2026', whereas DFML implements the swap from 2027-01-01 (US-MAS5-012): CONFLICT, open question. s.13 new c.62C s.90: an individual IRC amendment affecting MA gross income does not apply in the taxable year of its enactment or earlier (decoupling from same-year federal changes). s.8 adds c.62 s.2(d)(1)(R) deduction for Pub. Operating level: PFML split = employer payroll withholding; c.62C s.90 = assessment/definition of MA gross income (affects which federal exclusions carry into MA wages).

instrument_name: AGO Fair Labor Division - Domestic workers (Domestic Worker Bill of Rights, c.149 s.190)
authority: Massachusetts Office of the Attorney General, Fair Labor Division
figure_or_rule_carried: Domestic workers (incl. au pairs, Capron v. AG 944 F.3d 9) get minimum wage and overtime; notice of rights required; written agreement before work for 16+ h/week (pay rates, schedule, deductions, benefits, termination notice; in a language the worker easily understands; keep 3 years); payroll records and paystubs kept 3 years; timesheet at least every two weeks for 16+ h/week; 40+ h/week: 24 h off weekly and 48 h monthly unless waived in writing; meal deductions only if voluntary, written, max actual cost up to 1.50 USD breakfast / 2.25 USD lunch or dinner; housing deduction only if voluntary and not required to live in, max 35 USD/week (1 person), 30 (2), 25 (3+). UI coverage for domestic employers at 1,000 USD cash wages per quarter (US-MAS5-022).
